considered.reasoning: This replaces the weak cash-quality leverage template with a stricter serviced-leverage test. critic_notes.rationale: Multiplying book-to-market by retained-earnings-to-assets is effectively a repackaging of the published retained-earnings-to-market decomposition of the value premium (Ball-Gerakos-Linnainmaa-Nikolaev) and of standard quality-times-value composites, so it is a near-rediscovery rather than a new cross-theme mechanism.

Both legs share `oancf` in the numerator, so the product mostly double-counts the level of operating cash flow (a known cash-flow-to-price/coverage effect) rather than isolating the claimed cheapness-conditional-on-solvency interaction.

The conditional gating of book-to-market on net working capital exceeding total debt is a genuinely distinct construction, though the indicator collapses all non-qualifying firms to zero (making the short leg a liquidity screen rather than expensive stocks) and the common `at` scaling in the comparison is redundant.

Conditioning value on the *trajectory* of leverage rather than its level is a defensible and reasonably novel interaction, but it partially overlaps the known net-debt-issuance/financing anomalies and the ratio's denominator makes it sensitive to asset growth.

Sales-to-price and low ROA are strongly positively correlated by construction, so the product largely re-expresses the well-documented profitability anomaly and the expected negative sign will be driven almost entirely by the ROA leg rather than any value-trap interaction.

The second leg is Sloan's accrual measure with a cosmetic switch of scaler from assets to liabilities, and the expected negative sign is internally conflicted because the earnings-yield leg pushes the opposite direction, leaving the predicted sign dependent on which component dominates.

This is a cosmetic variant of the archive's already-tested "Liquidity-Backed EBITDA Value" (identical EBITDA/market-cap leg, with wcap/at swapped in for (che−dlc)/lct, itself already used as the conditioning leg in "Working-Capital Secured Cheapness"), so it recombines two evaluated components rather than testing a new mechanism.

The construction is internally consistent and the trajectory-based distress leg (falling current liabilities/assets) is a genuinely different conditioning variable from the level-based liquidity legs already tested, though the second leg partially overlaps with known asset-growth/net-operating-working-capital accrual effects and its stand-alone contribution should be diagnosed.

Net working capital minus long-term debt scaled by market equity is essentially Graham's net-current-asset-value ("net-nets") / net-liquid-assets-to-price measure, a long-published value anomaly, and as a plain single ratio it is neither cross-theme nor novel.

The numerator double-counts short-term debt (dlc is a component of lct), and more importantly liabilities-to-market-equity is a market-leverage measure that both Bhandari (1988) and its high correlation with book-to-market imply should predict returns *positively*, so the stated negative expected sign contradicts the expression's natural direction.

NEG(MA(pi,3))/market-cap is just a sign-flipped smoothed pretax earnings-to-price ratio, i.e., a direct rediscovery of the E/P anomaly rather than a distress-conditional interaction, since it is monotone in earnings yield across all firms and not confined to loss-makers.

The dividend-yield leg is a substantively different valuation anchor from the earnings/EBITDA/book legs already tested and the payout-sustainability conditioning is economically coherent, but the mass of zero-dividend firms will create heavy rank ties and effectively make the signal a payer-only sort, which needs to be checked before reading the coverage and spread diagnostics.

This is essentially the enterprise-multiple (EBITDA/EV) anomaly of Loughran-Wellman and a near-mechanical relabeling of the archived Creditor-Claim Earnings Yield (same denominator construction, ib swapped for ebitda), which already delivered a null FF5 alpha.

Conditioning high book-to-market on improving ROA is the core of Piotroski's (2000) F-score value screen, so the signal is a direct rediscovery of a well-published anomaly rather than a new cross-theme mechanism.

The construction is internally consistent and avoids using profitability as the distress leg, but the expected positive sign is questionable because high net-working-capital-to-sales is also a classic marker of inventory/receivable bloat and working-capital accruals, which predict *lower* returns and could offset the intended effect.

This is a cosmetic swap of the solvency leg in the archived Solvent Dividend Value (wcap/lt → (oancf-dvc)/lct) with the same anchor and hypothesis, and dividend-coverage screening is itself a long-standing practitioner signal, so it adds little incremental information beyond the already-tested weak result.

It is effectively the sign-flipped, mildly re-scaled version of the archived Persistent-Loss Deep-Value Trap and the fourth variant of the same book-to-market × balance-sheet-liquidity family (Working-Capital Secured Cheapness, Long-Runway Book Value), all of which produced negative or unreliable FF5 alphas, so it does not diagnose why the family fails.

It builds on the archive's one genuinely successful anchor (EBITDA yield) with a substantively different dynamic leg and a coherent sign, though the falling-net-liabilities term partly overlaps the known net-debt-issuance and asset-growth anomalies, so any result will need decomposition to show the interaction adds beyond those.

This is the archive's best performer (Liquidity-Backed EBITDA Value) with RANK mechanically swapped for IND_RANK — a cosmetic normalization variant rather than a substantively different mechanism, and it re-tests an already-evaluated construct.

Internally consistent and economically coherent, but it is essentially the winning EBITDA-liquidity composite with the numerator swapped to operating cash flow, so the incremental information content is modest and coverage will be thin (~0.09) given oancf availability.

The dlc/lt maturity-concentration leg is a genuinely different construct from the already-tested lct/lt version, but the close cousin (Long-Runway Book Value) produced a reliably wrong-signed FF5 alpha (t=-3.2), so the prior evidence argues against the hypothesis and the proposal does not address why.

Coverage stability is a genuinely new dimension (second moment rather than level of liquidity) that is not a rescaling of any archived leg and the sign logic matches the expression; the main risk is coverage loss and staleness from requiring five periods of oancf/lct history.

Legitimate and sign-consistent, but (act-lct)/lt is nearly identical to wcap/lt already tested in Solvent Dividend Value and is only a denominator swap on Operating-Liquidity Sales Value, so this is a re-scaling refinement with limited novelty.

The multiplicative form is internally incoherent for a negative expected sign — the low end of the product includes expensive-sales firms with severe cash burn (likely poor performers), so the composite is not monotone in the hypothesized trap dimension and a low-minus-high spread mixes contradictory economics.

This is a cosmetic variant of the archive's best performer (Liquidity-Backed EBITDA Value), swapping (che − dlc)/lct for (che + oancf)/lct, which re-uses the same EBITDA-yield × near-term-liquidity interaction and additionally blends in the already-tested OCF-yield channel rather than testing a new mechanism.

(at − lt)/lt is a monotone transform of book leverage, so the signal is simply cash-flow-to-price double-sorted on low leverage — two long-published anomalies multiplied together, with no mechanism beyond what the archive's several "value × solvency level" variants already probed.

Because RANK(NEG(oancf/lct)) is essentially the reverse rank of RANK(oancf/lct), the MIN-spread collapses to a monotone interaction of sales-to-price with OCF coverage — i.e., a sign-flipped restatement of the archive's already-tested and weak Cheap-Sales Cash-Coverage Spread.

The conditioning variable Δ(wcap/revt) is effectively the working-capital accruals anomaly, so the signal is accruals × sales-to-price, and the MIN construction reduces to the same interaction form already tested (and failed on FF5 alpha) in Supplier-Pressure Relief Sales Value; it also sits in direct tension with the archive's premise that high working capital is a cushion.

Replacing the one-period liability change in the archive's Net-Liability EBITDA Improvement Value with its acceleration is an incremental derivative of an already-tested conditioner whose FF5 alpha was significantly negative, and the MIN-spread wrapper adds no information beyond the equivalent product interaction.

Testing the change rather than the level of the (che − dlc)/lct cushion is a genuinely different economic mechanism (distress resolution vs. static safety) that could plausibly reconcile the archive's strong level result, though the MIN-spread wrapper is effectively just the rank product and the change-vs-level upgrade remains a modest step.

Because the two indicators are complements, the expression collapses to rank(EBITDA/ME) × sign((che−dlc)/lct), i.e. a coarsened binary version of the already-tested "Liquidity-Backed EBITDA Value" (fmb 5.0, alpha 5.1%), so it is a cosmetic discretization of the archive's best signal rather than a new mechanism.

Internally consistent and a substantively different conditioning leg (cash-flow coverage rather than a cash stock or its volatility/change, all of which were tested), though the strong mechanical correlation between ebitda and oancf means much of the interaction may just re-weight the valuation leg by 1/lct.

Consistent construction with a genuinely new conditioning variable (current-asset composition) not present in the archive, but it flirts with the known cash-holdings premium and ignores the liability side that drove the archive's successful (che−dlc)/lct legs.

This is a value-leg swap of the immediately preceding proposal, and che/act is close to the inverse of the working-capital-asset share already tested via revt/ME × (act−lct)/revt, (act−lct)/lt and TS_RANK(−lct/act), so it adds little independent information.

The liabilities-to-market valuation anchor is a genuinely new leg for this archive (all prior signals used ceq, ebitda, oancf, revt, or dvc over ME) and the coverage conditioning gives a coherent distress-premium-versus-equity-stub story, with the caveat that lt/ME overlaps Bhandari-style leverage and is mechanically tied to book-to-market.

Since the indicators are complements, this reduces to rank(revt/ME) × sign(oancf), which is the same monotone claim as the archived "Cheap-Sales Cash-Coverage Spread" (fmb −1.28, negligible alpha) with the sign convention merely reversed, so it is a relabeled retest of a failed signal.

This is a cosmetic temporal-smoothing variant of the archive's best performer (Liquidity-Backed EBITDA Value, same EBITDA/ME × (che−dlc)/lct construction) with TS_MIN(...,3) substituted for the contemporaneous level, and it will mainly reduce coverage rather than test a new mechanism.

The conditioner is an interpolation between two already-tested archive conditioners ((che−dlc)/lct in Cash-Buffered OCF Yield and che/act in Cash-Quality OCF Yield) applied to the identical OCF-yield anchor, so it is a denominator/numerator tweak rather than a substantively different hypothesis.

It is close to the archive's failed Creditor-Claim Earnings Yield template and edges toward a plain cash-flow-to-enterprise-value multiple, but the MAX(dlc, lct−che) shortfall adjustment is a genuinely different functional form (a single levered yield rather than a rank interaction) with defensible sign direction and high coverage, so it is worth one test.

It bolts a conditioner already shown to be near-useless in the archive (dlc-share of liabilities, e.g. Long-Runway EBITDA Value with ls_alpha −0.002) onto the proven che/act conditioner via SUMRANK, which most likely just dilutes the known effect rather than isolating anything new.

The stated "weaker of two safety dimensions" logic fails because MIN is applied to unranked ratios on very different level scales (che/lct typically well below ceq/lt), so the conditioner will almost always collapse to cash-to-current-liabilities and the expression does not compute the hypothesized weakest-link comparison.

A modest but legitimate cross-check of whether the strong che/act cash-composition conditioner generalizes from the OCF anchor to the higher-coverage EBITDA anchor (0.14 vs 0.079), which is an untested pairing with a real coverage-driven motivation rather than a pure relabeling.

This is a numerator swap (oancf → ebitda) on the already-archived "Loss-Runway OCF Yield" — same name, same runway ratio, and it also overlaps heavily with the archived Cash-Quality EBITDA Value, so it is a cosmetic variant rather than a substantively new mechanism.

The only change from the archived Cash-Quality EBITDA Value (fmb 5.11, alpha 5.8%) is adding lct − che to the denominator of an already-successful filter, a denominator tweak unmotivated by any diagnosed failure and therefore a cosmetic refinement of a strong incumbent.
